correctness.rationale: Exact completion of logistic square yields u'=−u²/K−p(u)y and y'=(p(u)−p0)y. Any nonextinguishing positive trajectory must have u>0, ∫u² finite and ∫u infinite. The exact z=u²/y linear equation with A(u)=(2−alpha)u/K+O(u²) yields a contradiction for alpha≤2 by its integrating factor bounded below. For alpha>2 a quadratic wedge has strictly inward upper boundary and reciprocal Riccati bounds prevent finite contact; the rational witnesses satisfy admissibility and are checked symbolically. These are analytical all-time proofs, not extrapolations from finite tests.

value.rationale: The maximal single-prey logistic yield h=K/4 is an intrinsic ecological boundary at which the predator-free equilibrium is degenerate. The exact derivative threshold identifies whether every nonzero initial predator forces finite-time prey exhaustion or a positive-measure initial-condition region yields prey survival despite the ongoing maximum harvest. It separates outcomes in the nonmonotone group-defense parameter family, supplies exact rational witnesses and an invariant example wedge, and is not a normalization check or routine local eigenvalue computation.
